subtype: Talks to teddy and feeds the doll [Actor]
passage: In the courtyard, two-year-old Ganga sat on the mat with her rag doll and a steel spoon. "Hungry," she told the doll, and pushed the spoon at its stitched mouth. "Aaah." Farhan, the neighbour's boy, leaned over the low wall. "Dolls don't eat." Ganga frowned and fed it again. She laid the doll on the charpai, pulled a small towel over it and patted. Pat, pat, pat. "Sho," she whispered. Her grandmother, shelling peas, smiled and hummed a lullaby.

qa.q: What did Ganga use to feed her rag doll?
qa.a: A steel spoon.

qa.q: What does Ganga's whispered "Sho" suggest she wants for her doll?
qa.a: She feels caring and tender toward the doll, wanting it to rest the way she herself is put to sleep.

qa.q: How could Farhan join Ganga's game instead of correcting her?
qa.a: He could pretend to feed or cover the doll too, which lets Ganga keep practising care.

qa.q: How does Ganga's grandmother see the game?
qa.a: She smiles and hums a lullaby, treating the feeding and patting as sweet, natural play worth supporting 😊

grounding: A toddler tells her doll it is hungry, feeds it and pats it to sleep, practising care through play.

subtype: Talks to teddy and feeds the doll [Actor]
passage: Thabo, two and a half, marched his teddy into the kitchen of their Durban flat. "Teddy hungry," he told his mum, Lucia. She handed him a cracker. Thabo held it to the bear's nose, said "Mmm," and nibbled it himself on Teddy's behalf. Then he found a shoebox, lined it with a dishcloth and laid the bear inside. He patted its tummy three times, the way Lucia patted his. "Night night, Teddy." He tiptoed away, finger on his lips.

qa.q: What did Thabo line the shoebox with?
qa.a: A dishcloth.

qa.q: What does Thabo tiptoeing away with a finger on his lips suggest?
qa.a: He feels protective of Teddy, believing the bear is sleeping and wanting to keep things quiet for its rest.

qa.q: Which small choice by Lucia helped the game along?
qa.a: Handing Thabo a cracker when he said Teddy was hungry, going along with the pretend care instead of correcting it.

qa.q: How might Lucia feel seeing Thabo pat the bear three times?
qa.a: She may feel touched to see Thabo copy the way she pats him and pass the same care on to his teddy.

grounding: A toddler says his teddy is hungry, "feeds" it and puts it to bed, copying the care he receives.

subtype: Talks to teddy and feeds the doll [Actor]
passage: My little sister Vidya is two. Tonight I watched her from the top bunk. She held her toy cup to her cloth elephant's trunk and said, "Drink, drink." Then she wiped its trunk with her sleeve. She laid it on her pillow and pulled the blanket up to its ears. "Ellie tired," she told me, very seriously. I don't know if she really thinks Ellie is tired. Maybe she's copying Amma. But she patted it so gently. Raghav, 9

qa.q: Where did Vidya put the elephant?
qa.a: On her pillow, with the blanket pulled up to its ears.

qa.q: What does Vidya saying "Ellie tired", very seriously, suggest?
qa.a: She is treating the toy as a being with feelings that needs rest, and she takes her caring job seriously.

qa.q: How could Raghav support the game if Vidya asks for help?
qa.a: Raghav could join in, for example by whispering goodnight to Ellie, which encourages the gentle care Vidya is practising.

qa.q: Why can't Raghav be sure what Vidya thinks about Ellie?
qa.a: Raghav only sees what she does; she might believe Ellie is tired or simply be copying Amma, and at two she can't explain it.

grounding: An older sibling watches a toddler give her toy elephant a drink and tuck it into bed.

passage:
Monday. Yamini, two, dragged her teddy to the kitchen. "Teddy hungry." She held a biscuit to its mouth, then ate it herself.
Wednesday. At nap time she laid Teddy on her pillow, pulled her hanky over him and patted. "Sleep, sleep."
Saturday. Her brother Vaibhav had a cold and lay on the sofa. Yamini brought Teddy, tucked him beside Vaibhav, and patted them both.

qa.q: What did Yamini pull over Teddy at nap time?
qa.a: She pulled her hanky over him.

qa.q: Why might Yamini have tucked Teddy beside Vaibhav?
qa.a: She seemed to want to comfort her poorly brother, using the same caring she had practised on Teddy.

qa.q: How could a parent join Yamini's teddy game?
qa.a: A parent could ask whether Teddy is full or sleepy and play along, since the game lets her practise caring.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav feel when Yamini brings Teddy and pats them both?
qa.a: He would probably feel cheered and a little amused to be cared for by his little sister.

grounding: A toddler feeds her teddy and puts it to bed, practising care she later offers her brother.

subtype: Talks to teddy and feeds the doll [Actor]
passage: On the balcony of their Chennai flat, Ayesha, two, sat her rag doll in an empty flowerpot. Keerthana Chithi was stirring rasam inside. "Baby hungry!" Ayesha shouted. She scooped air with a toy spoon and pushed it at the doll's mouth. "Aaa. Good girl." She wiped its chin with her frock. Then she laid it on the mat, covered it with a hand towel and patted, frowning like Chithi. "Shh. Baby sleep now."

qa.q: Where did Ayesha sit her rag doll?
qa.a: In an empty flowerpot on the balcony.

qa.q: What does Ayesha frowning like Chithi while patting the doll suggest?
qa.a: She seems happy and caring as she copies how Chithi looks after her, trying out being the one who cares for someone.

qa.q: How could Keerthana Chithi respond to the doll game?
qa.a: She could come out and ask if baby ate well or whisper so baby can sleep, encouraging the caring play.

qa.q: What might Keerthana Chithi think seeing her own frown on Ayesha's face?
qa.a: She might be amused and touched to see Ayesha copying her care so closely.

grounding: A toddler feeds her doll and puts it to bed, treating it as a feeling being in caring play.
